entries.english:
14 April 1500, Krumau. Peter von Rosenberg confirms the privileges granted in 14[?]8 by Ulrich von Rosenberg to the villages of Kaltenbrunn, Schild, Stein and Schlagt on Rossberg.

CCXCIII. I, Peter von Rosenberg, in my name and that of my brothers, heirs and successors, declare publicly by this letter, before all who see it or hear it read, that our faithful subjects from Kaltenbrunn, Schild, Stein and Schlagt beneath Rossberg appeared before us and reported that they had been granted town law by our noble and highly honored grandfather Lord Ulrich von Rosenberg, of glorious memory, and had received his sealed charter for it. Through careless keeping, however, that charter has become somewhat damaged and torn, so they are not adequately secured for the future in the enjoyment of that grant as they ought to be. They humbly asked us to allow them to retain the grant and renew the above charter, which they brought and laid before us; it is written word for word in German as follows: [Charter no. CCVIII follows.] Having considered the earnest and humble petition of the said faithful subjects, and wishing that the above villages, which lie on the border, be better provided for and prosper with their inhabitants, we have, after due deliberation and counsel, renewed and confirmed their above charter, grant and law. By the authority of this present instrument we graciously renew and confirm it, so that the said law and grant, through us, our brothers, heirs and successors, shall be securely and effectively observed for the said subjects and all their successors for all time, without opposition or any hindrance. In confirmation and testimony of this, with our certain knowledge, we have ordered our own great seal attached to this letter. Given at Krumau on Tuesday after Palm Sunday, in the year 1500.

From a copy certified by the town council of Krumau on 21 April 1684.
